title: 1969 AHSME Problem 33
statement: Let \(S_n\) and \(T_n\) be the respective sums of the first \(n\) terms of two arithmetic series. If \(S_n:T_n=(7n+1):(4n+27)\) for all \(n,\) the ratio of the eleventh term of the first series to the eleventh term of the second series is:

solutions.text:
For an arithmetic sequence, the eleventh term is the average of the first \(21\) terms. Thus the respective eleventh terms are \(\frac{S_{21}}{21}\) and \(\frac{T_{21}}{21}.\) Their ratio is \[ \frac{S_{21}}{T_{21}} =\frac{7(21)+1}{4(21)+27} =\frac{148}{111} =\frac43. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: In an arithmetic sequence, the middle term of the first \(21\) terms equals their average
Express each eleventh term as its corresponding \(21\)-term sum divided by \(21\)
